pairs.locus: Henry of Settimello, Elegia 3 (Liber III), lines 708-709, 777-778
pairs.question: Cur retulisti: "inmundus mundus que tibi munda dabit"?
pairs.answer: Iure vides igitur quod recta ligatio nectit "inmundus mundus" hec duo verba simul.
pairs.derivation: Henry asks Fronesis (Wisdom) to explain her earlier line (cf. l. 588 "Inmundus mundus que tibi munda dabit?"). Framing dropped: the speech tag "Tunc ego" and the meta-narration of the asking "Dic tamen ‚ unde supra memini bene ‚" ("Tell me — whence I recall well above —"). The same speech also asks a separate, unanswered question ("mundus an hic vene deterioris erit... stabit in esse suo?", ll. 704-707), so that part is excluded as it is not what the reply addresses; only the genuinely-answered "cur retulisti" interrogative is kept. First word capitalized; trailing punctuation normalized to "?". For the answer, the reply's non-answering preamble ("Vix umbram gerit hoc...", l. 711) and the long body of examples on the world's degeneration (gold-to-dung, corrupt curia, sale of the sacred, etc., ll. 711-776) are cut; the operative answering sentence is the closing summary (ll. 777-778) that directly states why the world is rightly called "inmundus mundus."
